title: transparent-slot-mediator-and-soft-cutoff-recovery
author: Priya Nandakumar
release_notes: Introduces a transparent slot mediation layer to reduce oscillations during regional load-shedding and a soft-cutoff recovery path that gradually relaxes tenant SLO constraints after transient overloads. Backwards compatible runtime flags control rollout.
description: Context: during a recent incident we saw aggressive tenant slot revocations when regional node pressure spiked; that produced cascading rejoin storms and prolonged elevated tail latency for mixed workloads. This PR introduces a transparent slot mediation layer (SlotMediator) that intermediates between the scheduler and the eviction/drain machinery and a soft-cutoff recovery path that: 1) enforces a short, metric-driven SLO relaxation window per-tenant instead of immediate slot release; 2) applies an exponential decay to per-tenant priority weights so hot tenants don't immediately reclaim capacity and destabilize the region; 3) emits rich telemetry for debugging and post-mortem. Motivation: the goal is graceful degradation with predictable recovery to avoid oscillation and reduce degradation surface area for bursty tenants. High level change: SlotMediator holds candidate evictions for a configurable quiet-window, probes local KV cache pressure and tail-latency signals, and either commits the eviction or relegates the tenant to a soft-cutoff state with temporarily reduced concurrency tokens. The soft-cutoff path keeps requests flowing with lower throughput (degraded but useful) while allowing the system to recover. Key safety: mediator decisions are deterministic given the same inputs, and a short-circuit emergency path bypasses mediation under critical per-node memory or disk pressure. Checklist: - [x] design doc updated (ENG-1987) - [x] unit + integration tests for mediation logic - [x] telemetry + dashboards added - [x] feature flag gated rollout - [x] staged canary in us-west-2 2-node cluster - [x] load test with synthetic tenant spikes Summary of user-visible behavior: - No API changes. - Under overload, tenants may be placed into a soft-cutoff state (reduced concurrency tokens) instead of immediate eviction. - Dashboard shows mediation decisions and per-tenant recovery timers. Rollout: start feature-flag false by default; enable in Canary region for 48h; if SLOs stable, progressively enable in remaining regions with 1h ramp per region. Downsides & trade-offs: prolonging degraded execution increases token cost slightly for a short window, but reduces tail-latency spikes and rejoin churn. Implementation notes: SlotMediator is lightweight and resides in the scheduler process; it subscribes to the same health and KV-pressure streams as the eviction controller and holds an in-memory LRU for candidate slots with TTLs. The soft-cutoff uses existing concurrency token plumbing but applies a decay multiplier defined by config.soft_cutoff_decay. Back-compat: all feature flags default to off and the emergency bypass remains unchanged.
commits: 3 commits: (1) Add SlotMediator core and config structs; (2) Integrate mediator with eviction controller and expose feature-flag toggle; (3) Telemetry, tests, and docs. Commit messages: 'slot: add SlotMediator and mediation policy', 'evict: wire mediator into eviction flow, add emergency-bypass', 'telemetry: emit mediator_decision, tests: mediation unit/integration, docs: rollout notes'
review_conversation: Reviewer Ethan: 'Can we avoid keeping long-lived in-memory state that could cause OOM if someone crafts a churny tenant?' Reviewer Lara: 'How were the decay constants chosen?' Author Priya: 'Chosen via bench runs in benchmark-lab: 0.6 initial multiplier with exponent 0.9 decay; included notes in docs and a flag to tune. Added integration test covering decay path.' Reviewer Samir: 'CI flagged a flake in integration test during a large synthetic spike.' Author Priya: 'Fixed race in test harness by adding explicit wait for telemetry flush; re-ran CI and green.' Approvals: Ethan approved, Lara requested one small doc wording change (addressed), Samir approved after CI fix.
ci_summary: CI matrix: unit (pass), integration (pass after fix), lint (pass), benchmark-lab smoke (pass). One transient integration failure on first run (resolved). E2E canary job executed in us-west-2 with simulated tenant spikes; observed 35% reduction in eviction churn and 18% lower 99th latency during recovery window.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: soft-cutoff prolongs degraded execution and could increase overall token spend. Mitigation: strict TTLs, exponential decay for reclaiming tokens, telemetry-based auto-disable if cost delta exceeds configured threshold. Risk: mediator could mask a true disk/memory OOM condition. Mitigation: emergency bypass that ignores mediator decisions under node-critical signals. Risk: misconfiguration during rollout. Mitigation: feature flag, config validation, and automated rollback in canary pipeline.
observability_changes: Adds 'mediator_decision' counter (decision=[commit|soft_cutoff|bypass]), per-tenant 'soft_cutoff_seconds' histogram, and dashboard 'Mediator overview' with heatmap of mediation events, eviction churn, and decay multiplier trendline.
deployment_instructions: Deploy order: 1) ship code to main behind flags; 2) enable telemetry dashboards; 3) enable feature-flag in canary region; 4) watch mediator_decision and 99p latency for 48h; 5) staged global enable with 1h per region roll. Rolling back: flip feature-flag false, monitor for immediate drop in soft_cutoff counts, then revert if necessary.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash on main. Changelog entry created under 'runtime' with brief note. Post-merge actions: run canary enable job and notify SRE channel.
notes_for_postmortem: Instrumented additional fields to aid future postmortems: decision_trace (string ID), pre_eviction_kv_pressure, pre_eviction_node_mem_pct. These are written to structured logs and linked to traces for any mediation event marked 'commit' or 'soft_cutoff'.
qa_notes: Integration tests simulate both KV pressure and tail-latency signals; added a fuzz scenario to ensure mediator doesn't deadlock. Manual QA performed using benchmark-lab spike harness; documented thresholds used for deciding success.
